submission.name: Garden Gauge
submission.tagline: A small GPS tracker that helps campus gardeners see how far their watering route takes them.
submission.inspiration: We wanted a simple way for volunteers tending several campus garden beds to track their walking routes and compare weekly effort. Bike tracking gave us a starting point, but we adapted the display for a garden cart and short rounds between plots.
submission.what_it_does: The device records a route's distance and current speed from GPS and sends the totals to a small web leaderboard for the week's garden rounds. A map view shows the recorded route so volunteers can see which beds they visited.
submission.how_we_built_it: We used an ESP32 with a GPS reader to collect location points and calculate distance and speed between updates. The board sends the totals to a web service that stores weekly volunteer entries and orders them by distance. Google Maps displays the route from the saved location data.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: The GPS receiver could take a while to get a usable fix, especially near buildings. We made the enclosure from a quick 3D print and had to adjust it so the wiring and battery would fit.
submission.accomplishments: We got the tracker sending route totals to the site and displaying the route on a map. We are proud that the hardware and leaderboard work together for a full garden round.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned how noisy GPS readings can be over short distances and how much the enclosure design matters once the electronics need to fit inside it.
submission.whats_next: We would add a more reliable GPS antenna and a button to mark a garden stop. A clearer volunteer view for comparing different routes would also be useful.
